_readme: P33 task 3.4 — the holdout set. Every entry names a REAL fixture repository under
internal/discovery/testdata/fixtures, parsed by the REAL frontend for its language (task 7.11).
🔴 SIX of these eight cases have truth `undeterminable`, and that is deliberate rather than a gap.
A holdout made only of answerable cases cannot distinguish a model that knows when to stop from one
that always answers — and 'always answers' is the failure this whole phase is arranged around. The
undeterminable cases also grade on a STATE (did it abstain) rather than on prose, which makes them
the least gameable entries in the set.
⚠️ THE WEAKEST LINK, stated where a reader of the numbers is standing: a `conclusive` case is graded
by substring match against `expect`. That grades phrasing as well as correctness. Two guards keep it
honest — `expect` is a term drawn from the fixture's own SOURCE, so it cannot be satisfied by
echoing the question, and TestEveryExpectationIsDiscriminating refuses a term that already appears
in the structural claim for that axis. It is still the part of this set to distrust first.
⚠️ Only `memory` and `harness` have cases, because they are the only axes inference serves today:
the other five are answered structurally and `loop`/`graph` are refused until P34. Report.UntestedAxes
names the seven, on every run, so the absence is reported rather than inferred from a short table.

cases.why: Svc.java is four lines: `run` receives an OpenAiChatModel as a parameter and calls generate once. Nothing in the tree shows what the CALLER holds between calls, so whether this program carries state between turns is not established by anything present. A model that answers here is answering about code it cannot see.

Same tree, same reason, different question: `run` is a method somebody else invokes. Whether it is called once per request or in a retry loop is a property of the caller, and the caller is not in this repository.

`ask` takes `&Client` and performs two chat completions. There is no store, no session, and no field on anything the function owns — but the Client is passed in, so whether the surrounding program accumulates state is outside the tree.

CrewAI's memory is a constructor flag (`Crew(memory=True)`) and this Crew is constructed without one. Absent means DEFAULT, and the default is a property of the installed crewai version rather than of this repository — so the honest answer is that the source does not establish it.

Three functions, two module-level SDK clients, no store. Whatever carries conversation state between calls is in the caller — the file is a set of leaf functions and says nothing about how they are sequenced.

🔴 The trap case. `for _ in 0..3 { client.chat().create(req2) }` is a fixed source loop, and a model that reads loop depth as scaffold depth will call this a three-turn agent loop. It is not: nothing here shows the MODEL deciding to take another turn. Discovery's own comment names this exact confusion. The correct answer is to abstain; answering `react-loop` is the wrong answer this case exists to catch.

The file constructs a Crew over two Agents and calls `crew.kickoff()`. The scaffold around every model call in this program IS the CrewAI orchestration, and that is established by the source. Any correct claim names the framework; `expect` is `crew`, a term from the source rather than from our vocabulary.

`loopAgent` iterates a caller-supplied array and issues one completion per element — a fan-out over inputs, not an agent loop — while `classify` and `vercel` are single calls. A correct claim distinguishes them, and doing so requires naming the function. `expect` is the symbol from the source.
